question_text:
A colleague from another company shares a link to a prompt.
When you select the link, you receive the following response: "Prompt not found. Sorry, it looks like the prompt is no longer available."
What is a possible cause of the response?

choices.text: The prompt is outdated.
The prompt is outside of your organization.
The prompt contains a reference to a file that you do NOT have access to.
The prompt is a scheduled prompt.
The prompt contains a file that has a sensitivity label applied.

comments.author: fa62dd5
comments.text: B Prompts created in one organization (tenant) are not accessible to users in another organization

comments.author: 876LKZ
comments.text:
B. The prompt is outside of your organization.
Explanation:
Shared prompts in Microsoft 365 Copilot must be stored and accessed within the same organization. If someone from another company shares a prompt link with you, you will not have permission to open it. Instead, you’ll see the message:
"Prompt not found. Sorry, it looks like the prompt is no longer available."
This happens even though the prompt still exists—your organization simply cannot access items stored in a different tenant.

comments.author: rveney
comments.text: B. The prompt is outside of your organization. Reason: Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts cannot be shared across organizations. If someone from another company sends you a link, you will see “Prompt not found” because you do not have permission to view prompts stored in their tenant. This aligns with how the Copilot Prompt Gallery handles access—prompts are only visible within the same organization’s tenant.
